target_customer: Grocery chains and retailers that order highly perishable foods
problem: Grocers over-order or under-order perishables, causing waste and lost sales. Shelf Engine predicted order quantities and automated ordering.
business_model: Automated ordering service for grocers where Shelf Engine took on risk for unsold goods and earned fees on sales
product_category: AI demand forecasting and automated ordering for grocery

founders.name: Stefan Kalb
founders.background_notes: YC page says Shelf Engine scaled to over 10,000 grocery locations and exited in 2024. A profile page says he ran Molly's for seven years and saw food waste there.

founders.name: Bede Jordan
education: QUT Brisbane, degrees in electrical and software engineering
founders.background_notes: From the company team page as shown in search results.

technical_complexity.rationale: Per-store, per-item forecasting for short shelf life goods is standard machine learning with hard parts in data integration, ordering execution and financial risk.

defensibility.rationale: Store-level sales data and ordering integrations built over time make it harder to switch, but forecasting software is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Planning vendors existed but the company grew to thousands of locations; it was eventually bought by Crisp in March 2025.

market_need_then: A report cited in sources puts grocery at about 10 percent of US food waste, 43 billion pounds a year, and perishables have thin margins, so waste cuts matter. This is a later industry statistic, not a 2018 measure.

branding.domain_note: shelfengine.com now redirects to the acquirer, Crisp.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission language about reducing food waste through automation

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive name and food waste mission, but no source on brand pull or community; growth came from sales to grocers.

outcome_analysis: Shelf Engine grew from a 2018 YC company to more than 10,000 grocery locations per its founder bio and raised a 12 million dollar Series A and a 41 million dollar Series B. The company had layoffs in 2022 and was acquired by Crisp in March 2025 for undisclosed terms, a real but not clearly large outcome.
notes: A seed from Initialized Capital in February 2017 is reported only in one snippet, so it is not recorded as a round. An aggregator lists a 2 million dollar Series B extension in September 2021, unverified. The YC page bio states over 70 million dollars raised, which exceeds the two rounds recorded, so the history is partial. Founder education beyond Bede Jordan was not found. No competitor with a dated source near 2018 was found; Afresh was founded in 2017 per an aggregator but no dated 2018 source was opened, so the list is empty. Layoffs in 2022 are from a search summary of GeekWire.
